studies.title: The Wick in the Candle of Learning: Epistemic Curiosity Activates Reward Circuitry and Enhances Memory
studies.verification_note: Bibliographic metadata and the short abstract excerpt checked against the publisher page. Abstract-level curation only; no full-text, correction-registry or independent replication review is claimed.
studies.permission_basis: Minimal attributed excerpt and original project summary; not a full-text mirror.
studies.source_text: We scanned subjects with functional magnetic resonance imaging while they read trivia questions.

findings.quote: We scanned subjects with functional magnetic resonance imaging while they read trivia questions.
findings.summary: Trivia-task curiosity covaried with reward-related activity, willingness to expend resources for answers, and later recall. These observations do not test cooking-video openings.
findings.population: Human participants reading trivia questions in laboratory imaging/behavioral tasks.
findings.outcome: Neural activity, answer-seeking resource expenditure and later recall.
limitations: Abstract-level curated summary, not a systematic review.
Different task, population, intervention and outcome from social video distribution.
Neural covariance and curiosity ratings do not establish a mediator in a creator's audience.

studies.title: Lighting the wick in the candle of learning: generating a prediction stimulates curiosity
studies.verification_note: Primary article metadata, abstract and Results/Discussion checked on PMC. The overall memory contrast between conditions was not significant; curiosity association is distinct from that contrast.
studies.permission_basis: Minimal attributed excerpt and original project summary; not a full-text mirror.
studies.source_text: More facts received high-curiosity ratings in the prediction condition

findings.quote: More facts received high-curiosity ratings in the prediction condition
findings.location: Abstract, fourth sentence (partial); interpretation reviewed against Results/Discussion
findings.summary: Generating numerical predictions rather than examples increased reported curiosity. Curiosity related to later recall, but overall memory did not significantly differ between the conditions.
findings.population: Laboratory numerical-fact learners; not social-video viewers.
findings.exposure: Generate a numerical prediction versus generate a relevant example.
findings.outcome: Self-rated curiosity, pupil responses and later recall.
limitations: The excerpt alone is not evidence for every paraphrased result; the recorded review also consulted Results/Discussion.
Overall memory improvement from prediction versus example was not established.
No cooking, platform retention, recommendation distribution or psychological mediation was tested.

constructs.definition: A desire to resolve an acknowledged knowledge gap; a proposed explanation, not a detected viewer state.
exclusions: A finished-dish image alone is not a curiosity measurement.
A positive comment or longer watch time does not distinguish curiosity from sensory appeal or utility.

operationalizations.procedure: Propose a separately authorized study using reviewed curiosity self-report items and a matched information-gap manipulation; validate adaptation before use.
operationalizations.population: Proposed consenting cooking-video viewers; not collected by SocialDNA.
operationalizations.indicator: An explicit curiosity measure and differential response to knowledge-gap manipulation.
limitations: A planning specification, not observed mediator data or a validated scale.
A creative variant effect alone does not establish the construct.
